value.body: A tutor helps school students with their subjects outside school hours, at the student's home, in a local tuition centre or online. Parents, coaching centres and online tutoring platforms hire tutors. A typical day is a few afternoon and evening batches: going over the day's lessons, practice work, and revision before tests.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: Subject knowledge; a teaching qualification such as D.El.Ed helps

items.label: Where the work is
items.value: Home tuition, local tuition centres, online tutoring platforms

items.label: Students taking private coaching
items.note: Taking or had taken coaching in the current academic year; higher in cities
items.source: NSO Comprehensive Modular Survey: Education (as reported)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Many start by tutoring neighbourhood children or joining a local tuition centre; online platforms usually take a subject test and a demo class. No licence is needed, but a teaching qualification and clear explanations help win parents' trust.

value.title: At a glance
items: Income depends on the number of students and is often seasonal, rising before exams.
Many tutors teach alongside a school job or while preparing for TET and recruitment exams.
Some go on to run their own tuition centre.
